In an event that signals a fundamental shift in Africa’s telecommunications market, Airtel Nigeria has launched the Airtel Open Network, a data-transparent digital platform on the My Airtel App that gives subscribers visibility into network coverage, signal strength, and service performance. The platform which was unveiled on Friday, 30 October, 2026 before an audience of key industry stakeholders led by the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission, Dr. Aminu Maida, media partners, and corporate executives in Lagos makes Nigeria the first of Airtel Africa’s 14 operating markets to introduce the level of consumer-facing network accountability. The Open Network feature, which is now live on the My Airtel Africa App to all Airtel subscribers, shows via visual icons, the 4G and 5G sites, sites being upgraded, and coming sites within a 500-metre radius of a customer’s location. Addressing the regulators and industry leaders during his keynote address, Chief Executive Officer of Airtel Nigeria, Dinesh Balsingh, said customers deserved clearer information about the network they depend on and the work being done to improve it. “Trust grows when customers can see what is happening and know that their concerns are being heard. With Open Network, we are giving customers greater visibility into our network and a more direct way to tell us where their experience falls short,” Balsingh said. This is about making network information easier to access and understand, not asking customers to interpret complex technical details on their own,” he said. In his special remarks, Dr Maida highlighted the importance of accessible information and appreciated the effort by Airtel to strengthen consumer confidence. “Open Network by Airtel is an initiative that can complement the work we do at the NCC. The Commission’s assessment of service quality will continue to be guided by evidence and the standards that apply across the industry. This is why we expect operators to keep improving beyond minimum requirements, including addressing persistent service challenges, as Airtel is demonstrating with this initiative.” Airtel leadership highlighted that transparency must coexist with technical clarity. A coverage indicator does not guarantee uninterrupted reception under all conditions, as indoor penetration, structural barriers, handset specifications, and localised network congestion naturally influence individual experience. “Open Network does not, by itself, resolve every service issue or automatically change network performance,” Balsingh noted. “What it offers is a superior starting point for understanding available information and raising concerns clearly when experience differs from expectations. Sustained operational investment is what improves network performance; information is what builds trust.” The launch marks the commencement of a nationwide educational campaign. Airtel Nigeria said it will roll out practical demonstrations and user guides across digital, retail, and traditional media channels to onboard its tens of millions of subscribers onto the platform.
